title: PARTITION BY
description: PARTITION BY splits the rows into groups for the window function, restarting the calculation within each group - unlike ORDER BY alone, which treats every row as one big sequence. Write a query that returns each employee's `first_name`, `department_id`, `salary`, and their salary rank WITHIN their own department (1 = highest paid in that department), using ROW_NUMBER.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: PARTITION BY
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) alone would rank every employee against the whole company - adding PARTITION BY department_id resets the numbering back to 1 at the start of each department.
Select first_name, department_id, salary, and a ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by department_id and ordered by salary descending, from employees whose department_id isn't NULL.
expected_behavior: Returns one row per employee that has a department, with a salary rank that restarts at 1 in each department.
solution: SELECT first_name, department_id, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dept_rank FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL;
explanation: PARTITION BY is to window functions what GROUP BY is to aggregates - except the rows stay ungrouped, so you still get one output row per employee, each carrying its own rank.
